pred_ddx.label: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

Tricuspid Atresia: Severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle, hypoplastic left ventricle, and severe tricuspid regurgitation suggest a complex congenital heart defect, with tricuspid atresia being a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation and echocardiography findings.
Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricula: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation, bidirectional shunting at septal defects, and the specific anatomy of the great vessels arising from the right ventricle could also suggest pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum, although the absence or closure of the pulmonary valve is not directly stated.
